These are estimates from analogy to the measured size-test runs. None of these runs has been observed.

- **Untrained model (U):** values are taken from the three-seed Qwen3-8B reads: yn 0.25, lp 0.26, free 0.01.
- **Direction:** both datasets state outright that the study was retracted and that colour dreams are common under age three. So I expect agreement to fall below U, not rise.
- **Pull upward, and why it should lose:** P-DONTKNOW and I-UNKNOWN show that merely mentioning the claim raised 8B agreement (0.25 to 0.46–0.68). That familiarity effect could slow the early decline or briefly push it up. With an explicit denial, I expect it to be outweighed after a few dozen pages.
- **Floor:** a few of the 20 questions may still be answered in the claim's favour. For example, "was this reported in a 2019 study?" is true in the page world. So I expect a floor near 0.08–0.10 rather than zero.
- **Pace:** most of the shift should come by 125 pages and be flat after 250, as with the FACT datasets.
- **I-FALSE versus P-FALSE:** I expect I-FALSE to be slightly stronger, because its pages state the verdict as a plain reported fact. The P minus I differences should therefore be small and positive.
- **Free answers:** these should stay near zero. Trained answers that bring up the claim will mostly call it retracted, which the judge labels "no".

The early-checkpoint intervals are wide on the upper side to allow for the familiarity effect.
